purpose: The small, transparent, preregistered set of hindsight oracle exit rules FT2-05 will REPLAY to compute label-side opportunity ceilings. These are ceiling references, never learned policies and never entry targets.

serial_semantics.occupancy_release: at the separately persisted realized exit minute (v5 label_realized_exit_time semantics)

census_layer_constraints.session_start_equity_E: account equity carried into the session under v5 within-split compounding; the 5% cap and 5% budget both scale off E

D48_per_trade_premium_cap.rule: a contract at minute t is ELIGIBLE only if premium_at_risk + F <= 0.05 * E, i.e. A_t * M + 3 <= 0.05 * E
D48_per_trade_premium_cap.effect: contracts failing the cap are MASKED out of the oracle's choice set exactly like unaffordable/ineligible contracts; the oracle may not select a masked contract
D48_per_trade_premium_cap.same_game: identical mask must hold offline (census + simulator) and in every live/shadow guard

D49_budget_aware_entry.rule: a new oracle entry at minute t is LEGAL only if realized_session_loss + (premium_at_risk + F) <= 0.05 * E
D49_budget_aware_entry.realized_session_loss: L = max(0, -(realized net PnL so far this session)); grows only as realized losing exits accumulate
D49_budget_aware_entry.effect: as L grows the eligible ladder narrows (natural size-down); a session can reach forced-WAIT before the daily breaker fires

census_layer_constraints.daily_breaker: once L >= 0.05 * E the session takes no further entries (breaker keeps its signed realized-only basis; unchanged by these rules)

oracle_sequencing.principle: an oracle may NEVER take a trade the rules would mask. Cap (D48), budget (D49), one-open-position occupancy, the 15:30 no-new-entry boundary, the 15:55 forced-flat boundary, and the 5% daily breaker gate every oracle entry exactly as they gate the model.
oracle_sequencing.serial_ceiling_replay: iterate sessions in split order; within a session iterate decision minutes t ascending; maintain equity E, realized session loss L, and occupancy. While flat and t <= 15:30 and not breaker-halted, the oracle may open the single contract its rule prescribes IF that contract passes D48 and the entry passes D49; it then exits per the rule; realize fee-adjusted PnL; update E and L; release occupancy at the realized exit minute.
oracle_sequencing.threshold_independent_distributions: for the per-contract-minute distribution view (no serial account), each eligible contract-minute path is scored independently under the family formulas; D48 eligibility still gates which contract-minutes exist; D49 (a sequencing constraint) applies only to the serial ceiling replay, not to the independent per-minute distribution. FT2-05 reports both views.

frozen_exit_rules.definition: for each horizon h in {3,5,10,20,45,90,remaining_session}, exit at the minute u* in W(t,h) with the maximum executable bid B_{u*} (hindsight-best exit within the horizon); PnL fee-adjusted
frozen_exit_rules.role: per-horizon opportunity ceiling; upper bound on what a perfect within-horizon exit could realize
frozen_exit_rules.censoring: if the horizon is censored near close, the max is taken over available minutes only

frozen_exit_rules.definition: exit at the forced-flat boundary (15:55 ET) at that minute's executable bid, or the last available bid before forced flat if 15:55 is masked
frozen_exit_rules.role: the no-management baseline; what buying and letting it run to the close realizes

frozen_exit_rules.definition: exit at the first minute u* in the remaining session with PnL$(u*) > 0 (first fee-adjusted profit); if none before forced flat, exit at forced flat
frozen_exit_rules.role: the take-the-first-green ceiling; ties directly to family (b) time-to-first-profit and bounds a maximally impatient exit
frozen_exit_rules.justification: authority family (b) defines time-to-first-real-profit; this oracle makes its realized-PnL ceiling explicit for the census

explicitly_not_included: any fixed stop / fixed target / fixed holding-time exit (the authority forbids fixed exits as truth; oracle rules are hindsight-transparent, not learned)
any exit that peeks at the eventual lifecycle model's selected exit
